Xi Jinping has arrived in North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years, as China’s leader looks to revitalise ties with his junior ally.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

India declares onset as up to 280mm of rain falls in 72 hours in Kerala, while downpours hit south-west Thailand

rfi.description: Former Uefa president Michel Platini said on Monday he is suing Fifa president Gianni Infantino, in the latest chapter of a battle that began when scandal derailed Platini's 2015 bid for the Fifa presidency. After unsuccessful attempts in Switzerland, Platini is now turning to the French justice system to make his case.

rfi.description: French NATO fighter jets stationed in the Baltic region shot down a drone that had entered Latvian airspace on Monday, marking a rare interception under the alliance’s Baltic Air Policing mission. It follows a series of similar incidents linked to the war in Ukraine as Moscow and Kyiv step up drone strikes on each other.

euronews.description: US forces carried out strikes against Iran on Wednesday in what President Donald Trump said was retaliation for the downing of an American helicopter by the Islamic Republic a day earlier.

euronews.description: Thousands of people gathered in Paris to demand accountability and reforms after the killing of 11-year-old Lyhanna, criticising the handling of the case by French authorities and the justice system.

euronews.title: Archaeological sensation: Iron Age Celtic grave discovered in Hesse
euronews.description: During surveys for a solar park in Hesse, archaeologists uncovered a Celtic princely tomb with exceptional grave goods near Bad Camberg, a find of European significance, according to Hesse’s state archaeologist Udo Recker.

euronews.title: El Niño is set to bring extreme weather this summer. Here’s what it means for travellers
euronews.description: The UN’s World Meteorological Organisation now warns there is an 80% chance El Niño develops this summer.

euronews.title: Spain: Thousands gather as Pope Leo XIV reaches Barcelona
euronews.description: Spain's Barcelona welcomed Pope Leo XIV on 9 June as thousands gathered for a prayer service at the city's cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulalia. The pontiff's visit includes a landmark ceremony at the Sagrada Familia Basilica.

euronews.title: EU targets Russia's Patriarch Kirill in new sanctions proposal
euronews.description: Patriarch Kirill, the head of Russia's Orthodox Church, is among the many names included in the latest proposal of EU sanctions against Russia.

euronews.description: The new ranking from AirHelp looks at on-time performance, facilities and overall airport experience.

euronews.description: The European Environment Commissioner told Euronews that Brussels must "connect the dots" and understand that environmental, economic and security interests go hand-in-hand.

euronews.title: Kaja Kallas urges Ireland to clarify alumina sales to Russia
euronews.description: Ireland has launched an investigation into allegations that exports from Aughinish Alumina have contributed to Russia's military complex.

euronews.description: The move by Paris comes as the UK, Canada and Norway intensify sanctions on settlement-linked organisations and financial networks accused of supporting violence in the occupied West Bank.

euronews.description: The trial is the latest case aimed at delivering justice after a series of similar thefts in libraries across Europe, allegedly by an organised network.

euronews.title: Spain’s Sánchez speaks out against EU's deregulation crusade
euronews.description: As socialists discuss how to regain ground across Europe, the Spanish prime minister has rejected the idea that fewer laws are needed at the European level, putting him at odds with the simplification push led by Germany and Italy.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump se résout à frapper l’Iran pour préserver sa crédibilité
lemonde.description: L’armée américaine a mené une action « proportionnée », mardi soir, en réponse à l’attaque qui a abattu un hélicoptère Apache près du détroit d’Ormuz. Mais le président américain, qui espère toujours un accord avec Téhéran, évite pour l’instant l’escalade.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : le gouvernement sous le feu des critiques à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Entre demande de moyens à gauche et appels à des mesures plus répressives à droite, l’affaire a monopolisé, mardi, les débats parlementaires. De leur côté, les candidats à la présidentielle formulent des propositions pour réformer l’institution judiciaire.

lemonde.title: Au Collège de France, un faux détecteur de fumée pour filmer les femmes aux toilettes
lemonde.description: Un agent administratif du CNRS a été condamné à dix-huit mois de prison, mardi 9 juin, pour des faits de voyeurisme à caractère sexuel à l’encontre de dizaines de scientifiques d’un laboratoire de recherche en biologie.

lemonde.title: En Californie, vers un duel entre un démocrate et un républicain pour le poste de gouverneur
lemonde.description: Historiquement à gauche, l’Etat verra s’affronter, lors des élections du 3 novembre, le démocrate Xavier Becerra et le républicain Steve Hilton. Selon les responsables des élections, le premier a reçu 27,9 % des voix et le second 25 %, lors des primaires.

lemonde.title: A Belfast, des manifestants anti-immigrés incendient des bâtiments et des véhicules au lendemain d’une attaque au couteau imputée à un réfugié soudanais
lemonde.description: Les habitants d’un immeuble en feu ont dû être évacués. Des figures d’extrême droite, comme le militant Tommy Robinson, avaient lancé sur les réseaux sociaux des appels à manifester.

lemonde.title: France-Irlande : les Bleues viennent à bout des Irlandaises et arrachent leur qualification pour la Coupe du monde de football 2027
lemonde.description: L’équipe de France a souffert pour battre l’Irlande (1-0) et terminer en tête de son groupe, mardi 9 juin à Grenoble. Une victoire due à Melvine Malard, auteure d’un but spectaculaire, et à la gardienne Constance Picaud-Inconnu, tout en efficacité.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky affirme avoir obtenu le résultat escompté de sa lettre ouverte à Vladimir Poutine
lemonde.description: « J’avais un objectif en envoyant cette lettre à Poutine, et je pense avoir obtenu le résultat dont j’avais besoin », a déclaré de manière volontairement sibylline le président ukrainien. Le 4 juin, il avait adressé une lettre ouverte à son homologue russe, lui proposant une rencontre en tête-à-tête.

lemonde.title: SNCF : en pleine « crise existentielle », les cheminots sont appelés à la grève
lemonde.description: Les syndicats CGT, CFDT, SUD-Rail et UNSA, qui dénoncent les conditions de travail et les salaires, appellent le personnel à débrayer le 10 juin.

lemonde.title: Afghanistan : les talibans dispersent un rassemblement de femmes en tirant sur la foule
lemonde.description: Les forces de sécurité du régime islamiste ont ouvert le feu sur une foule rassemblée, le 9 juin, pour protester contre l’arrestation de plusieurs femmes accusées de ne pas porter le hijab intégral correctement.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, un budget de 70 milliards de dollars pour la lutte contre l’immigration approuvé par la Chambre
lemonde.description: Le texte prévoit notamment un financement de 38 milliards de dollars pour la police de l’immigration (ICE), et d’environ 26 milliards pour la police aux frontières (CBP).

lemonde.title: En Algérie, le voile de la colonisation obscurcit toujours les relations : « Les Français croient nous connaître, mais ils se trompent »
lemonde.description: « Les mémoires blessées de la guerre d’indépendance » (3/3). Les traumatismes demeurent chez les survivants et les descendants des victimes de la guerre. lemonde.title: « La victoire de Nikol Pachinian en Arménie devrait encourager la stabilisation d’un régime démocratique »

lemonde.title: Au moins treize civils tués en Afghanistan lors de frappes pakistanaises

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Karim Bouamrane se lance dans la course en revendiquant une « ligne claire » contre LFI

france24fr.description: Le principal accès au stade Aztèque de Mexico, où doivent se tenir jeudi la cérémonie et le match d'ouverture du Mondial 2026, a été bloqué plusieurs heures mardi par des milliers d'enseignants qui manifestent depuis la semaine dernière. La présidente Claudia Sheinbaum a exclu pour l'heure de donner l'ordre à la police de réprimer les manifestations.

france24fr.title: Les Bleues battent l'Irlande et se qualifient pour le Mondial 2027 au Brésil
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France féminine de football ira au Brésil pour la Coupe du monde 2027, après sa qualification mardi soir face à l'Irlande du Nord grâce à un but acrobatique de Melvine Malard.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Adidas va-t-il humilier Nike chez lui ?
france24fr.description: La Coupe du Monde 2026 se joue sur le sol américain, le bastion de Nike, et Adidas a une chance historique de lui prendre son marché, son image et sa domination. Les deux marques ont déjà sorti leurs armes : campagnes marketing aux stratégies opposées, guerre des maillots officiels, éditions limitées et activation digitale à échelle mondiale. Décryptage avec Jonathan Lumbroso, ex-directeur marketing d'Alven, l'un des premiers fonds d'investissement tech en France, et fondateur d'iytro.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : Un arbitre somalien refoulé à Los Angeles
france24fr.description: Il s'appelle Omar Artan. Il est Somalien et avait été désigné meilleur arbitre africain l'an dernier. Pourtant, il a été refoulé samedi à son arrivée aux États-Unis. La FIFA s'est résignée et a annoncé qu'il n'officierait pas durant la Coupe du monde de football. En Somalie, c'est l'indignation.

france24fr.title: Kim Jong-un embarrasse-t-il la Chine ?
france24fr.description: Le président chinois, Xi Jinping, a bouclé mardi son déplacement en Corée du Nord. Il a été accueilli en grande pompe lundi par Kim Jong-un, à l'occasion de sa première visite dans le pays depuis 2019, à l'heure où Pyongyang s'affirme aux côtés de Moscou et maintient fermement le cap sur son programme nucléaire.

france24fr.title: Affaire Patrick Bruel : "La justice avait largement de quoi enquêter et avancer" dès 2019
france24fr.description: Alors que Patrick Bruel est entendu depuis lundi dans une enquête sur des faits d'agressions sexuelles et de tentatives de viol qui concernent une dizaine de femmes, les critiques se concentrent sur le traitement des premiers signalements reçus par la justice dès 2019. Témoignages concordants, faits non prescrits, victimes jamais auditionnées : des spécialistes s'interrogent sur les occasions manquées d'approfondir les investigations.

france24fr.title: La Patrouille de France dessine le drapeau tricolore au-dessus de la statue de la Liberté
france24fr.description: Pour le coup d'envoi de la mission française, baptisée "Liberté 250", dans le cadre des célébrations du 250e anniversaire de la Déclaration d'indépendance des États-Unis, huit appareils de la Patrouille de France ont survolé la statue de la Liberté, offerte par la France en 1886.

france24fr.title: Afghanistan : la police afghane disperse violemment une manifestation de soutien aux femmes
france24fr.description: La police de l'Afghanistan, pays dirigé par les Taliban, s'en est pris à des manifestants mardi, venus défendre la liberté des femmes afghanes. Une vague d'arrestation a été lancée trois jours plus tôt par la police des mœurs du gouvernement taliban, parce que des habitantes de Herat ne portaient pas le tchador ou la burqa, qui couvrent entièrement le corps, mais juste un voile.

france24fr.title: Violentes manifestations anti-immigration à Belfast après une attaque imputée à un réfugié
france24fr.description: Malgré les appels au calme de la police d'Irlande du Nord des violentes manifestations ont éclaté à Belfast, après l'arrestation mardi d'un Soudanais dans le cadre d'une agression au couteau qui a laissé un homme d'une quarantaine d'années dans un état grave. Des personnalités d'extrême droite britanniques avaient appelé à des manifestations anti-immigration.

france24fr.title: Les banques financent toujours trop les hydrocarbures (ONG)
france24fr.description: Les banques du monde ont encore augmenté leurs investissements dans le secteur des énergies fossiles en 2025. C'est la conclusion du rapport "banking on climate chaos", publié par un groupe d'ONG. Le document délivre en revanche un satisfecit aux banques françaises qui, à rebours de la tendance internationale, ont réduit leurs investissements dans le secteur. Selon l'AIE, pour réussir la transition énergétique, il faudrait réduire le financement des énergies fossiles de 60% par an d'ici 2030.

france24fr.title: La Russie a-t-elle abandonné la très disputée flèche de Kinbourn aux portes de la Crimée ?
france24fr.description: Selon des médias ukrainiens, les forces russes ont commencé à quitter la flèche de Kinbourn, un petit bout de terre à l’ouest de Kherson qui a été l’un des lieux les plus stratégiques du début de la guerre d’invasion russe à grande échelle en 2022. Et maintenant ?

france24fr.title: Ebola : un homme abattu lors d'un soulèvement contre un centre de quarantaine pour Américains au Kenya
france24fr.description: La police kenyane a abattu un manifestant alors que des centaines de personnes organisaient mardi de nouvelles manifestations contre un centre de quarantaine au Kenya, destiné aux Américains exposés au virus Ebola. Les protestataires estiment que le pays n'est pas "une décharge" pour les Américains malades et préfèrent qu'ils soient soignés aux États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : les violences xénophobes se multiplient
france24fr.description: Les manifestations xénophobes continuent en Afrique du Sud. Des affrontements ont eu lieu ce lundi dans une petite ville dans la province du Cap. Dans une adresse à la nation, le président Cyril Ramaphosa a demandé la fin de ces violences et annoncé des mesures concrètes, mais ses propos n'ont pas convaincu les étrangers.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : France, Espagne, Argentine… Qui sont les favoris et les outsiders ?

observador.description: As preocupações do Banco Mundial focam-se, sobretudo, nos choques que Moçambique sentiu com as cheias que vivenciou no início deste ano, mas também com o impacto da guerra no Médio Oriente.

observador.title: Ação judicial contra mina da Borralha em Montalegre
observador.description: A Povo e Natureza do Barroso avançou com uma ação sobre a Declaração de Impacto Ambiental do projeto mineiro que obteve parecer favorável da APA em janeiro.

observador.title: IA para criar enzimas que degradam plásticos
observador.description: Doutorado em Química pela Universidade do Porto, Alexandre Pinto usa inteligência artificial para desenhar enzimas que degradam plásticos, com foco no PET e outras classes.

observador.title: Papillon, Sam The Kid e Slow J fecham Sol da Caparica
observador.description: O festival lusófono decorre de 13 a 16 de agosto na Costa da Caparica. Passes de quatro dias para residentes de Almada já estão esgotados.

observador.title: Chega diz que há casas "abandonadas" na Terceira
observador.description: Seis habitações na Terra Chã foram emparedadas pelo Governo Regional. O Chega promete requerimento na Assembleia para apurar responsabilidades políticas.

observador.title: Temperaturas sobem até 40°C esta semana em Portugal
observador.description: De 10 a 13 de junho, Portugal continental vai sentir uma massa de ar quente e seco vinda do norte de África. Sexta-feira é o dia mais crítico.

observador.title: Complexo do Boavista tem licitação, Bessa não
observador.description: Desde 20 de abril, o estádio e o complexo dos "axadrezados" estiveram eletronicamente à venda no sítio oficial da Leilosoc na Internet, mas só o segundo ativo imobiliário teve ofertas acima do mínimo.

observador.title: Ópera sobre Camões com estreia esta quarta-feira
observador.description: Com libreto da escritora Luísa Costa Gomes, a ópera é uma tragicomédia sobre Camões. O espetáculo afasta-se de uma homenagem estática para questionar a própria autoridade do cânone.

observador.title: Hoje é só disto que se trata
observador.description: Surpreendentíssimo é ter sido Leão XIV o primeiro “grande” a entrar em cena com o argumento da IA: sozinho, diante da plateia do mundo. Entre a esperança e o perigo, a vantagem e a desvantagem.

observador.title: Cuidado, senhores deputados
observador.description: O combate ao racismo é uma coisa desejável, mas é um perigo pôr na mão de pessoas como o SOS Racismo um articulado que lhes permita perseguir judicialmente quem tem ideias com que não concordam.

observador.title: Henry Nowak e o racismo anti-branco
observador.description: Num Ocidente dominado e subjugado pela vertigem da política identitária e do wokismo institucionalizado que a extrema-esquerda impôs, Henry Nowak não tinha a identidade correcta para ser vítima.

observador.title: Dia de Portugal com vinhos do Porto e Douro em Berna
observador.description: Exportações DOC Douro para a Suíça chegaram a 5,5 milhões de euros em 2025. Porto e Douro vendem acima do preço médio global no país helvético.

observador.title: Santos populares animam 12 bairros da Guarda
observador.description: A festa dos santos populares na Guarda, que começa na quinta-feira no quartel dos bombeiros voluntários, será um momento de convívio e de valorização das tradições, segundo a vereadora da Cultura.

spiegel.title: Mode und Style: Leena Zimmermann gibt Pack-Tipps für den Urlaub
spiegel.description: Leena Zimmermann stylt Stars wie Karoline Herfurth und Hannah Herzog. Hier verteidigt sie den Stil der Deutschen, spricht über Individualität in der Mode und gibt Packtipps für den trendsicheren Sommerurlaub.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz in Schulen: Warum Schule weniger abfragen und mehr zuhören sollte
spiegel.description: Spickzettel sind out, heute schummelt man in Klassenarbeiten mit ChatGPT. Irgendwie schamlos, denke ich. Vielleicht, weil der Betrug so mühelos wie unkreativ ist. Womit wir beim Bildungssystem sind.

spiegel.title: »007 First Light«: Ist dieses Game der beste Bond-Film aller Zeiten?
News: Friedrich Merz, FCAS, ILA, Benzin, Russland, Ukraine, Krim
spiegel.description: FCAS hin oder her – heute startet die Internationale Luft- und Raumfahrtmesse. Die Koalition trifft Gewerkschaften und Arbeitgeber. Und auf der Krim geht der Sprit aus. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochmorgen.

spiegel.title: Immobilien: Der Babyboomer-Effekt – wo die Hauspreise bald sinken könnten
spiegel.description: Wenn die Gesellschaft altert und die Bevölkerung schrumpft, dürften viele Immobilien bald günstig zu haben sein. Hier erfahren Sie, welche Regionen zum Schnäppchen werden und wo die Preise weiter steigen.

spiegel.title: Immobilien-Kauf: Wie wir uns den Traum vom Fachwerkhaus erfüllt haben
spiegel.description: In den Metropolen explodieren die Mieten, auf dem Dorf sind Immobilien günstig zu haben. Marie Timm und ihr Mann erzählen, wie es mit dem Landleben klappen kann. Und was daran nervt.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: US-Militär greift Ziele im Süden Irans an – Teheran reagiert offenbar mit Attacken in Golfregion
spiegel.description: Donald Trump macht das Regime in Teheran für den Verlust eines US-Kampfhubschraubers verantwortlich. Er wollte Vergeltung. Jetzt meldet das amerikanische Militär neue Attacken. Iran verkündet Gegenschläge auf US-Ziele.

spiegel.title: Wolfgang Kubicki (FDP) bei Sandra Maischberger: Scharfe Antworten kann er. Unscharfe aber auch
spiegel.description: Der neue FDP-Vorsitzende drängelt sich bei »Sandra Maischberger« mit harter Kritik am Kanzler in die Schlagzeilen, distanziert sich klar von der AfD – und wird ungenau, als es wirklich interessant wird.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Kongress bewilligt 70 Milliarden Dollar für umstrittene Migrationspolitik
spiegel.description: Donald Trump kann seine aggressive Abschiebepolitik bis zum Ende seiner Amtszeit durchsetzen: Nach dem Senat hat auch das Repräsentantenhaus der Finanzierung zugestimmt. Jetzt fehlt nur noch die präsidiale Unterschrift.

spiegel.title: Coronamasken: Textilfirma fordert halbe Milliarde Euro vom Bund
spiegel.description: Die Pandemie ist Geschichte, aber die finanziellen Folgen sind noch immer nicht ausgestanden. Ein Textilhändler fordert vor Gericht nun viel Geld für Coronamasken. Dabei geht es auch um die Rolle von Jens Spahn.

spiegel.title: Fast 600 bestätigte Ebola-Fälle in DR Kongo – USA fordern Restriktionen in Europa
spiegel.description: Die Zahl der Ebola-Infizierten in Zentralafrika steigt weiter, mehr als hundert Menschen sind bereits gestorben. Um Infektionen bei der Fußball-WM zu verhindern, fordern die USA Einreisebeschränkungen in Europa.

spiegel.title: Belfast: Nach Messer-Angriff eskalieren rassistische Ausschreitungen
spiegel.description: Mitten auf einer Straße in Belfast traktiert ein Messerangreifer sein blutendes Opfer, ein Video der Tat wird vielfach geteilt. Nun kam es in britischen Städten zu Demonstrationen – angefacht von Rechtsextremen.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz echauffiert sich über SPD - »Meine Geduld ist am Ende, auch mit den Sozialdemokraten«
spiegel.description: Seit Wochen ringen Union und SPD über Reformen. Weder bei Rente noch bei Pflege oder Steuern zeichnen sich Kompromisse ab. Bei einem Gesetz zu Bauvorhaben wirft der Kanzler dem Koalitionspartner laut einem Medienbericht nun Blockade vor.

spiegel.title: Anthropic: Umstrittenes KI-Modell Mythos nur eingeschränkt verfügbar
spiegel.description: Anthropic hat das umstrittene KI-Modell »Mythos« erstmals öffentlich freigegeben. Trotz nur eingeschränkter Version bleiben Bedenken vor militärischer Nutzung und möglichem Missbrauch für Cyberangriffe.

spiegel.title: »Spargelfahrt« der SPD: Noch bevor das Schiff ablegt, setzt Markus Söder das Zeichen
spiegel.description: Gleich vier Unionspolitiker gehen mit SPD-Abgeordneten an Bord eines Ausflugsschiffs. Sie haben Hintergedanken – vor allem CSU-Chef Markus Söder.

spiegel.title: Kubicki kritisiert Friedrich Merz bei »Maischberger« Erwartungsmanagement als »unterirdisch«
spiegel.description: Nach seiner Wahl zum FDP-Vorsitzenden übt sich Wolfgang Kubicki in außerparlamentarischer Opposition. In der ARD-Talkshow »Maischberger« wirft er dem Bundeskanzler Defizite in Kommunikation und Regierungsführung vor.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026:DFB-Spieler spendieren 600 Fans die Fahrt zum Stadion
spiegel.description: Das deutsche Team bestreitet sein drittes Gruppenspiel in New Jersey. Die Fahrt dorthin ist von New York aus aber enorm teuer, ein Zugticket kostet 98 Dollar. Nun springen die Spieler ein – aber nicht für alle Fans.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Serena Williams siegt bei Comeback in London an der Seite von Mboko
spiegel.description: »Ich war es leid, zu Hause rumzusitzen«, sagte Serena Williams nach ihrer Rückkehr auf die Tennis-Bühne. Die ehemalige Nummer eins der Welt gewann an der Seite von Victoria Mboko in London – und will bald nach Deutschland kommen.

elpais.title: El fracaso del caza europeo expone la debilidad de la defensa de la UE
elpais.description: El primer ministro belga, Bart de Wever, considera que el fiasco es una “pura estupidez”

elpais.title: España busca opciones ante el fiasco del futuro eurocaza: desarrollarlo con Alemania o comprarlo a Francia
elpais.description: Robles: “Se han impuesto los intereses de la industria a los de la seguridad europea y eso es grave”

elpais.title: Visto para sentencia el juicio a David Sánchez: un informe de la UCO contra medio centenar de testimonios
elpais.description: El tribunal tendrá que decidir si prevalece el documento policial en el que las acusaciones sustentan su relato o las declaraciones en la vista que afloraron la supuesta debilidad del mismo

elpais.title: Dirigentes del PSOE piden a Ferraz que se querelle contra Leire Díez: “Hay que lanzar un mensaje político”
elpais.description: Líderes territoriales y miembros de la Ejecutiva quieren trasladar que “no hubo ninguna connivencia” con la exmilitante. Ferraz no descarta ninguna acción judicial pero está “a la espera de los avances de la investigación”

elpais.title: Pedraz autorizó de urgencia el registro de un bajo a nombre de un conocido de Cerdán donde guardó enseres tras la mudanza desde Madrid
elpais.description: El magistrado accedió a que la UCO entrara en una segunda dirección en Navarra después de encontrar el contrato de la mudanza en su vivienda. El ex secretario de Organización del PSOE ha denunciado una persecución

elpais.title: Un rito sexual en el escenario y bombas de humo en la grada: medio siglo del primer concierto de The Rolling Stones en España
elpais.description: En un momento tortuoso para la banda y crítico para la Transición política, el grupo liderado por Mick Jagger y Keith Richards tocó en la Plaza de Toros Monumental de Barcelona en plena gira caótica y a 900 pesetas la entrada

elpais.title: Cómo buscar un sitio perfecto para ver el eclipse total: tres apps y una web resuelven el dilema
elpais.description: El teléfono móvil y la tecnología de realidad aumentada permiten comprobar con antelación si el Sol estará a la vista en la ubicación de su usuario el día 12 de agosto durante el fenómeno astronómico

elpais.title: Siete aperitivos de los mejores cocineros para hacer en casa y ver el Mundial de fútbol
elpais.description: La excusa es ver el partido de la selección favorita, pero siempre se disfruta más con un bocado para celebrarlo

elpais.title: ¿Qué queda por construir? Las dos manzanas de viviendas que necesita la Sagrada Familia para ser terminada
elpais.description: La expansión de Barcelona dejó al templo encasillado entre manzanas edificadas: donde ahora hay casas, están proyectadas una escalinata y una plaza. Aunque quizás Gaudí no las contemplaba.

elpais.title: El Mundial de la opulencia y los récords: precios disparados para ir a los estadios y accesos denegados para entrar en EE UU
elpais.description: La FIFA busca en la mayor y más mercantilizada Copa del Mundo de la historia, con 104 partidos y 48 selecciones, que el fútbol penetre de forma definitiva en Estados Unidos, un mercado con 350 millones de personas

elpais.title: Estos son los cinco jugadores más prometedores del Mundial 2026
elpais.description: Más allá de Lamine Yamal, que ya hace tiempo dejó de ser promesa, aquí una selección de algunos debutantes a seguir

elpais.title: La luz épica del estadio Azteca, por Jorge Valdano
elpais.description: Pelé y Maradona se consagraron como mitos sobre este césped. Y en sus gradas nació la ola, la coreografía colectiva que une aficiones rivales. Con el partido inaugural del 11 de junio se convertirá en el único estadio en albergar tres mundiales

elpais.title: Estados Unidos advierte a los ‘influencers’ extranjeros antes del Mundial: es ilegal crear contenido con una visa de turista
elpais.description: Nuevas regulaciones del Gobierno de Trump exigen que los creadores de contenido extranjeros porten un visado que les permita trabajar legalmente en el país

elpais.title: Estados Unidos ataca objetivos en Irán tras el derribo de un helicóptero
elpais.description: Washington “debe responder, necesariamente, a este ataque”, había advertido Trump. Los dos tripulantes del Apache han sido rescatados ilesos en una operación inédita

elpais.title: Marruecos impone su superioridad aérea en el Sáhara para quebrar la línea sucesoria del Frente Polisario
elpais.description: El ejército marroquí se ha equipado con drones israelíes y turcos para rechazar los avances saharauis por el desierto con ataques como el que ha matado a un alto dirigente

elpais.title: Cotrina, el líder del PSOE extremeño que ofrece un pacto al PP si echa a Vox: “Cerrarles la puerta es tener un clima social mejor”
elpais.description: El alcalde de Salorino, un pueblo cacereño de 500 vecinos, es la voz de los socialistas extremeños desde abril. Con 39 años, lanzó este martes un discurso contundente y fuera de lo común en tiempos muy polarizantes

elpais.title: Lo que nunca cambia sea quien sea el Papa: la Iglesia española sigue lejos de su autofinanciación
elpais.description: Pese al acuerdo entre el Estado y la Santa Sede hace 47 años que preveía su autonomía económica, la institución católica continúa dependiendo del Estado

elpais.title: León XIV se convierte en ídolo y referente de los católicos más jóvenes
elpais.description: Rafael Ruiz, profesor de Sociología de la UCM, analiza la normalización del catolicismo entre los jóvenes y los posibles efectos de la visita del Pontífice entre ellos

nyt.title: Steve Hilton Wins Second Spot in California Governor Race, Beating Tom Steyer
nyt.description: Steve Hilton, a Republican endorsed by President Trump, will face Xavier Becerra, a Democrat, in the general election. Tom Steyer, another Democrat, will not advance.

nyt.title: Sanders-Backed Progressive Advances in California Swing District Against Valadao
nyt.description: Randy Villegas will face the incumbent, David Valadao, a Republican who has survived numerous challenges in a competitive district.

nyt.title: Rep. Kevin Kiley, Independent, to Face Richard Pan in California House Race
nyt.description: Mr. Kiley dropped his Republican affiliation earlier this year. The newly drawn Sixth Congressional District is widely considered to be favorable for Democrats.

nyt.title: Lindsey Graham Wins Republican Senate Primary in South Carolina
nyt.description: Mr. Graham, a four-term incumbent, is the favorite to win the general election in a solidly Republican state.

nyt.title: Nevada Attorney General Wins Democratic Nomination for Governor
nyt.description: Aaron Ford easily outpaced a Washoe County commissioner, Alexis Hill, for the nod to take on Gov. Joe Lombardo in November.

nyt.title: Navy Admiral Fired by Hegseth Advances to Runoff to Replace Mace
nyt.description: Nancy Lacore would face a tough fall election in a district drawn in 2021 to be more Republican. She is seeking to replace Representative Nancy Mace, who ran unsuccessfully for governor instead of running for re-election.

nyt.title: Blanche Was Once Seen as Tempering Trump’s Tactics. Now He’s All In.
nyt.description: The ascendancy of Todd Blanche shows how the practices that were initially deemed out of bounds even in President Trump’s Justice Department seem to be the order of the day.

nyt.title: House Passes G.O.P.’s $70 Billion Immigration Bill
nyt.description: The vote gave final passage to Republicans’ megabill to fund immigration enforcement through the remainder of President Trump’s term, clearing it for his signature.

nyt.title: House defies Johnson and passes Democratic-led labor bill
nyt.description: Twenty G.O.P lawmakers broke with Speaker Mike Johnson and joined Democrats in backing a bill to amend the National Labor Relations Act.

nyt.title: Hannah Neeleman’s Ballerina Farm Store Draws Crowds in Utah
nyt.description: Tourists are flocking to Midway, Utah. The Ballerina Farm Store, from the influencer whose brand revolves around motherhood and farm life, is a reason.

nyt.title: Trump’s Sharp Turn on China: Embracing It as a Peer Power
nyt.description: President Trump’s warming with Xi Jinping of China, a leader he admires, has ignited anxieties in Washington and across Asia.

nyt.title: In the Hybrid A.I.-Human Work Force, Who Will Actually Thrive?
nyt.description: A panel of experts explains how job seekers should prepare for the future of work.

nyt.title: Anthropic Releases ‘Safe’ Version of Its Mythos A.I. Technology
nyt.description: Called Claude Fable 5, it is twice as expensive as the company’s previous flagship system.

nyt.title: Meta A.I. Bug Allowed Hackers to Take Over Instagram Accounts
nyt.description: The flaw, which Meta said it had fixed, allowed anyone to take over accounts using a bug in the company’s new artificial intelligence software.

nyt.title: Meet the NASA Astronauts in the Artemis III 4-Person Crew
nyt.description: NASA’s next mission in its effort to return humans to the moon will be led by an all-male crew. Three of them have extensive experience in space, while the other was a backup on Artemis II.

nyt.title: Can NASA Really Land Astronauts on the Moon by 2028?
nyt.description: Experts have been hopeful, but say the agency’s lunar aspirations are largely at the whims of two billionaires, Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos.

nyt.title: Paramount CEO David Ellison Pledges Editorial Independence for ‘60 Minutes’
nyt.description: David Ellison told Ms. Stahl, one of three remaining correspondents for the news program, that he would respect the show’s editorial decisions after a tumultuous stretch.

nyt.title: How Talking to the ‘Chat’ Crossed Over Into Real Life
nyt.description: It’s a word ripped from Twitch streams, but it functions as a Greek chorus for an online, isolated generation.

republika.description: Ogni sera in migliaia sfilano in sostegno ai pasdaran: ma la realtà per la popolazione è ben più dura: “Benessere e dissenso sono spariti”

republika.description:
Ieri è arrivato l’ordine di evacuare anche i quartieri che finora erano
stati risparmiati. Un fiume di auto si riversa lungo le strade che portano a nord

republika.description: La giornalista libanese: “Anche se è positivo che le autorità libanesi abbiano rotto il tabù del parlare direttamente con gli israeliani, tentando di separare il loro destino da quello di Teheran, non vedo pace all’orizzonte”

republika.title: Violenze sui palestinesi, l’Onu denuncia coloni e Hamas
republika.description: Un nuovo dossier sulle gravi violazioni subite dai civili intrappolati tra le forze israeliane e i coloni da un lato e Hamas dall’altro

republika.description: Le autorità aprono un’indagine penale: sarebbe il quarto alto ufficiale colpito a morte lontano dal fronte. Peskov: “Mediazione Usa in pausa”

republika.description: L’ex ministro degli Esteri di Kiev: “Non illudiamoci, l’Ucraina non sta vincendo la guerra. Però è messa meglio rispetto a 6 mesi fa”

republika.description: Il presidente dell’Anac: “Le norme hanno ridotto i controlli. Con una nuova gara l’iter sarebbe stato più trasparente”

republika.description: La vera questione è se l’Italia voglia realizzare un’opera storica seguendo il metodo della conoscenza e del rigore scientifico, oppure se preferisca “procedere all’incontrario”, confidando che i problemi possano essere affrontati più avanti, magari scaricandone i costi sui governi e sulle generazioni future

npr.title: President Trump says U.S. 'must' respond to Iran attack that downed Army helicopter
npr.description: Monday night, President Trump spoke optimistically about negotiations to end the war with Iran. Now, he has confirmed that Iran shot down a U.S. Army Apache helicopter, saying the U.S. must respond.

npr.title: 4 states head to the polls. And, global conflicts are on the rise, new report says
npr.description: Voters in four states head to the polls today for their primaries. Here are the races to watch. And, global conflicts are at their highest level since World War II, data shows.

npr.title: Conflicts around the globe hit highest levels since World War II, new report says
npr.description: The new report by the Uppsala Conflict Data Program said the massacres in El Fasher pushed one-sided violence in Africa to its highest levels since the Rwandan genocide in 1994.

npr.title: Global violence reaches record levels due to war and attacks on civilians
npr.description: Attacks on civilians have brought global violence to record levels. NPR's Leila Fadel talks to researcher Therése Pettersson at Uppsala University in Sweden.

npr.title: Conflicts are on the rise globally, at the highest level since WWII, data shows
npr.description: Global conflicts surged to the highest number tallied by Uppsala Conflict Data Program. Fatalities were the highest on record since 1994, with approximately 244,600 people killed in conflict in 2025.

npr.title: Sweden set to ban mobile phones in schools
npr.description: Long championed as a leader in adopting digital technology, Sweden is set to ban mobile phones in schools beginning in the fall for the next academic year.

npr.title: Trump vows to respond after Iran downed a U.S. Army helicopter near Strait of Hormuz
npr.description: A drone boat rescued two Army aviators who were aboard the Apache attack helicopter when it went down near the Strait of Hormuz.

npr.title: Pentagon labels tech giant Alibaba and car maker BYD as aiding Chinese military
npr.description: The Pentagon has added several prominent Chinese businesses to its list of Chinese military companies. The move prevents them from securing U.S. defense contracts.

npr.title: Federal judge strikes down Trump's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas
npr.description: A federal judge on Monday struck down the Trump administration's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas. The administration announced the fee as a way of preventing foreign workers from taking American jobs.

new-sci.description: A complex ecosystem of woolly mammoths, bison, horses and big cats has been elucidated by studying the faeces of small rodents that probably ate the bigger animals

new-sci.title: The last-ditch plan to save coral reefs from utter destruction
new-sci.description: Bleaching has devastated reefs around the world, raising fears of an irreversible shift. Yet new interventions have revealed that corals can be remarkably resilient if we can give them enough help to recover

new-sci.description: Physics is considered a cold, hard science – but it will transform your life if you view it with a bit more subjectivity, says Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.description: Brown dwarfs are somewhere between the size of a planet and a star, so how could we have potentially mistaken two of them for distant galaxies? Columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein argues that solving this cosmic mix-up is particularly possible now, as galaxy research has never been stronger

new-sci.title: Dinosaur-killing asteroid impact site stayed hot for millions of years
new-sci.description: Drill cores at the impact site of the Chicxulub asteroid show evidence that, alongside widespread destruction, the collision created a vast underground ecosystem filled with hot water that sheltered microbial life

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: You don't need to worry about recursive-self-improving AI – yet
new-sci.description: Anthropic has warned that recursive-self-improving AI could be on the horizon, but the truth is the company is more immediately concerned with marketing itself for a blockbuster initial public offering on the stock market, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. Columnist Michael Marshall examines how archaeologists are rethinking this critical part of our history

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

new-sci.title: Can Apple and Google stop children from sharing explicit images?
new-sci.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has warned tech firms, including Apple and Google, that they must voluntarily implement tools to stop children sharing explicit images, but experts warn this is easier said than done

new-sci.title: Half the world's reservoirs could be clogged up with dirt by 2060
new-sci.description: Each decade the world is losing over 7 per cent of its freshwater storage capacity to sediment build-up, according to an analysis of over half a million reservoirs

new-sci.title: Understanding anorexia’s grip on the brain could unlock new therapies
new-sci.description: One-third of people with anorexia nervosa don’t recover and treatment has remained stagnant for years. Now we’re beginning to understand how the condition takes over the mind

new-sci.title: You could get some of the benefits of sleep without having to nod off
new-sci.description: Mice seemed to reap some of the benefits of sleep by having their brain activity stimulated while they were awake, and the researchers plan to test the approach on people

new-sci.title: Are we getting to the point where it's safe to gene-edit babies?
new-sci.description: A team in the US has reported promising results after using an improved form of CRISPR to gene-edit human embryos, but a major issue remains unsolved

new-sci.title: The maths meme that has been distracting mathematicians for a century
new-sci.description: A seemingly simple set of rules kicks off a kind of mathematical magic trick, which has kept great minds busy since the 1930s. Columnist Jacob Aron explores the origins of the Collatz conjecture, why it is so addictive to mathematicians and whether AI could help us solve it once and for all

new-sci.title: Superintelligent machines may well need us after all
new-sci.description: Despite AI's dizzying improvements in mathematical ability, its successes show just how integral human mathematicians are to the scientific process

phys-org.title: To discover new physics, AI may need to 'unlearn' the old one
phys-org.description: A study in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics explores how a machine-learning strategy known as transfer learning could dramatically reduce the computational cost of searching for new physics beyond the standard cosmological model—while also revealing an unexpected risk: Sometimes AI systems can become too reliant on what they already know.

phys-org.title: Study finds fishing bycatch does not attract lesser black-backed gulls out of wind farms
phys-org.description: Lesser black-backed gulls from the colony on the Dutch island of Neeltje Jans appear to avoid the wind farm off the Zeeland coast, with the exception of some males. NIOZ ecologist Rosemarie Kentie and her colleagues suspected the gulls were attracted by fishing boats outside the wind farm and the bycatch thrown overboard. This turned out not to be the case: Even during weekends, when there is little fishing, the birds rarely visit the wind farm.

phys-org.title: Theoretical model developed to understand how isotopes change spectroscopy results
phys-org.description: When researchers want to uncover what atoms make up a material, they turn to a number of tried-and-true spectroscopy methods. Spectroscopy works by shining a specific type of light onto a substance and then analyzing how that light is either absorbed, emitted, or scattered. Every atom has a different way of interacting with light, and scientists study this light-matter interaction to identify the atoms in the material.

phys-org.title: Survival of five million amphibians and reptiles displaced by construction in British Columbia may not be tracked
phys-org.description: UBC researchers have found that more than five million amphibians and reptiles were displaced by development in British Columbia in just four years—and that there is no requirement to monitor survival rates. The paper published in the Journal of Wildlife Management is the first of its kind to document the large-scale herpetofauna relocation taking place in the province.

phys-org.title: How health care systems shape native preferences for immigrants
phys-org.description: In recent years, anti-immigration sentiment has become increasingly common around the world. A common concern surrounding immigration is its potential impact on the host country's welfare system, including health care. Such concerns can reduce public support for accepting immigrants and for redistributive welfare policies.

phys-org.title: Strong leadership will be key as AI reshapes the workforce, argues research
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence changes how work gets done, experts say strong leadership will play a critical role in helping employees adapt to shifting responsibilities, evolving technologies and changing workplace demands. The findings are published in the journal Human Resource Development Review.

phys-org.title: Physicists harness potential of quantum phase transitions
phys-org.description: Researchers at University College Dublin and international collaborators have just published a detailed and accessible guide that aims to translate theoretical ideas into practical devices for quantum enhanced sensing technologies.

phys-org.title: Satellite data reveal hidden labor trafficking in Brazil
phys-org.description: A Stanford team used geospatial data and detection algorithms to achieve a tenfold increase in rescues from modern slavery in the Brazilian Amazon. Now, they are planning to expand their approach.

phys-org.title: Examining doctoral students' attitudes toward AI chatbots and ChatGPT use in higher education
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies have published research examining graduate students' attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and their reported use of ChatGPT in higher education environments. The article, "Relationship between Students' Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence (AI) and their usage of AI Chatbots," appears in the International Journal of AI in Pedagogy, Innovation, and Learning Futures.

phys-org.title: How 'undone science' shaped Chile's glacier protection battle
phys-org.description: What is "undone science," and how does it affect environmental policy and regulation around the world? In a recent study published in Tapuya: Latin American Science, Technology and Society, Javiera Barandiarán, an associate professor in global studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and colleagues trace how undone science has shaped conflicts between mining and glacier conservation over the past two decades in Chile. phys-org.title: Neutron-rich nuclei yield beta-decay clues that could refine heavy-element origin models
phys-org.description: How are heavy elements formed in the universe? Extremely neutron-rich atomic nuclei and their beta-decay rates play an important role in this process. Until now, it has been very difficult to determine these rates experimentally. Researchers at TU Darmstadt have developed theoretical predictions for such processes and successfully compared them with experimental data, where they exist. The results were published in Physical Review Letters.

phys-org.title: NASA unveils Artemis III astronauts to test technology for a future moon landing
phys-org.description: NASA on Tuesday revealed the crew for its Artemis III mission, the next step in the space agency's plan to eventually land astronauts on the moon.

phys-org.title: Physicists observe synchronized quantum dance of excitons and phonons
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers has reported a major advance in understanding quantum dynamics in semiconductor materials. They directly observed how excitons and phonons evolve together in perovskite nanocrystals, revealing a fully coherent quantum dance between light-induced electronic excitations and crystal lattice vibrations. They published their findings in Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Quality of relationship between patient and therapist is key to preventing child sex offenders from doing it again
phys-org.description: Since the 1980s, there has been extensive research on the effectiveness of treatment for perpetrators of sexual crimes against children. Studies have examined rehabilitation programs, the role of clinicians and the factors associated with recidivism. However, what remains unclear is how these factors interact to influence recidivism once treatment is over.

phys-org.title: Freshwater boundary breach deepens as climate and land use amplify extremes
phys-org.description: Human activities have significantly altered the freshwater cycle, threatening its ability to support vital climatic and ecological Earth system processes. A new study led by researchers at the University of Eastern Finland shows that the freshwater cycle has increasingly moved away from a stable state due to climate change and large-scale water and land use. phys-org.title: Brain removal in Iron Age Scotland burial reveals far-reaching family ties
phys-org.description: It is difficult to identify funerary practices in Iron Age (c. 800 BC–AD 43) Britain, as human remains rarely survive. However, evidence is particularly prominent in north-west Scotland, because environmental conditions support the preservation of bone. To take advantage of this, a team of researchers from the U.K. and U.S. examined two individuals (one adult female and one juvenile male) buried in a low stone cairn at Loch Borralie in Sutherland, close to the north-west extremity of the Scottis

phys-org.title: Why vague conservation targets are failing some vulnerable species
phys-org.description: A shift toward more precise, measurable conservation goals could hold the key to protecting vulnerable species, according to the findings of a new study looking at African elephants. Conservationists are often faced with difficult decisions about where to put their financial resources; invest where populations are largest or where declines are fastest? Or invest in multiple smaller sites to maintain a species' range?

phys-org.title: Adélie penguins use colony cues to switch foraging sites if their previous trip was unsuccessful
phys-org.description: Many animals live in groups. Among seabirds in particular, most species form colonies during the breeding season. Although coloniality entails costs, such as increased competition for food and disease transmission, its repeated evolution across animal lineages suggests that group living provides important benefits.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power.
